scores.label: A
scores.note: Options 1 and 2 are vague and generic but usable. Option 3 gives the resilience to Ms. Alvarez, but the paragraph presents her as a helper, and 'sharing the resilience' reads oddly. Option 4 adds a claim the paragraph does not make: that helping new students builds resilience as a habit. Option 5 adds a vague, unsupported claim that resilience is 'the key to understanding'.

scores.label: B
scores.note: Option 3 adds a claim with 'I have always admired my resilience'. It is self-praising and out of tone for the paragraph. Option 4 stretches the 'first few months' to 'early years'. All five options follow the same 'my resilience helped' pattern.

scores.label: C
scores.note: Option 2 has muddled logic: resilience 'helps me remember' does not use the word correctly. Options 1 and 4 read like definitions and are awkward. Option 3 is the strongest.

scores.label: D
scores.note: No zeros. Options 3 to 5 drift a little: option 3 adds 'others also struggling with English', option 4 has an ambiguous 'which', and option 5 says 'the country'. They are still usable.

scores.label: E
scores.note: No zeros. Option 3 changes the stated reason for helping: the paragraph says 'because I know how it feels'. Option 2 credits resilience rather than the teacher for better reading and writing. Sentence structures vary well.
